position.claim: havdala is recited as an independent fourth blessing

segments.en: A tannaitic dispute is cited in the mishna with regard to the appropriate blessing in which to recite havdala within the Amida prayer. «Rabbi Akiva says:» Havdala «is recited» as an independent «fourth blessing.» Rabbi Eliezer says that it is recited in the seventeenth blessing of the Amida prayer, the blessing of thanksgiving. The first tanna says that it is recited in the fourth blessing of the Amida prayer: Who graciously grants knowledge.
segments.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אוֹמְרָהּ בְּרָכָה רְבִיעִית כּוּ׳.

position.claim: havdala is recited as an independent fourth blessing

segments.en: «MISHNA:» This mishna speaks of additions to the standard formula of the Amida prayer and the blessings in which they are incorporated. «One mentions the might of the rains» and recites: He makes the wind blow and the rain fall, «in» the second blessing of the Amida prayer, the blessing of «the revival of the dead. And the request» for rain: And grant dew and rain as a blessing, «in» the ninth blessing of the Amida prayer, «the blessing of the years. And the prayer of distinction [havdala],» between the holy and the profane recited in the evening prayer following Shabbat and festivals, «in» the fourth blessing of the Amida prayer: «Who graciously grants knowledge. Rabbi Akiva says:» Havdala «is recited» as «an independent fourth blessing. Rabbi Eliezer says» that it is recited «in» the seventeenth blessing of the Amida prayer, the blessing of «thanksgiving.»
segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ מַזְכִּירִין גְּבוּרוֹת גְּשָׁמִים בִּתְחִיַּית הַמֵּתִים, וּשְׁאֵלָה בְּבִרְכַּת הַשָּׁנִים, וְהַבְדָּלָה בְּחוֹנֵן הַדָּעַת. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אוֹמְרָהּ בְּרָכָה רְבִיעִית בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: בַּהוֹדָאָה.

checks.alternatives: Identical wording could reflect independent attestations. The explicit Mishnah heading here instead supports repetition; do not generalize beyond the havdala insertion.
checks.attribution: Both name Rabbi Akiva. The anonymous first opinion also uses the fourth blessing but incorporates havdala into knowledge, so it must not be conflated with an independent blessing.
checks.conditions: Both occurrences place havdala as an independent fourth blessing in the Amida; this is Rabbi Akiva's attributed position, not the accepted ruling.
checks.negation: Both affirm this placement; the other Mishnah placements are alternatives attributed to other parties, not denials by Rabbi Akiva.
checks.sourceIndependence: 33a24 is the abbreviated Rabbi Akiva heading of the Mishnah at 33a11. Preserve two extraction occurrences but count only one source statement.
